title: Cyclic Groups, Generators and Prime Order
quickIdea: A cyclic group is generated by one element: every element is a power of it. Z_n is the model, phi(n) counts its generators, and every group of prime order is cyclic.
remember: G is cyclic when G is the set of all powers of one element a, written G = <a>; a is then called a generator. Cyclic groups are abelian, and every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic.
(Z_n, +) is cyclic, generated by 1. Its generators are the residues a with gcd(a, n) = 1, so there are phi(n) of them.
A group of prime order p is cyclic, and every element other than the identity generates it. This is why groups of order 2, 3, 5 or 7 are automatically abelian.
A cyclic group of order n has exactly one subgroup of order d for each divisor d of n, and no other subgroups; so Z_12 has six subgroups.
Z_2 x Z_2 has order 4 and is not cyclic: every element other than (0, 0) has order 2, so no single element generates the group.
Z_2 x Z_3 is isomorphic to Z_6 and is cyclic, because gcd(2, 3) = 1. In general Z_m x Z_n is cyclic exactly when gcd(m, n) = 1.
The number of elements of order d in a cyclic group of order n is phi(d) for each divisor d of n, and 0 otherwise.

example.prompt: List the generators of Z_12 and show that 5 generates the whole group.
example.work: gcd(a, 12) = 1 for a = 1, 5, 7 and 11, so exactly these four generate. The multiples of 5 mod 12 are 5, 10, 3, 8, 1, 6, 11, 4, 9, 2, 7, 0: all twelve residues appear before 5 returns to 0.
example.answer: The generators are 1, 5, 7 and 11, which is phi(12) = 4 of them, and <5> = Z_12.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 Q.34 is the whole pattern: a group of composite order may or may not be cyclic, but a group of prime order always is. Any proper non-trivial subgroup of a group of order 6 has order 2 or 3, and both are prime.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Is every abelian group cyclic?
variations.answer: No: Z_2 x Z_2 is abelian of order 4 and is not cyclic, because every non-identity element has order 2.
variations.why: Cyclic implies abelian is one direction only, and Z_2 x Z_2 is the smallest counterexample to the converse.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: How many generators does Z_20 have?
variations.answer: phi(20) = 8: the residues coprime to 20, namely 1, 3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17 and 19.
variations.why: phi(20) = 20 (1 - 1/2)(1 - 1/5) = 8, and each of these residues generates the group.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: G is a group of order 6 containing an element of order 6. What is G?
variations.answer: G is isomorphic to Z_6, hence cyclic and abelian; the other group of order 6, namely S3, has no element of order 6.
variations.why: An element of order equal to |G| generates the whole group, so the group is determined up to isomorphism.

trap.what: Assuming a group of composite order is cyclic, or that every abelian group is cyclic.
trap.why: Order 6 splits into Z_6 (cyclic) and S3 (not); order 4 splits into Z_4 (cyclic) and Z_2 x Z_2 (not). Compositeness alone decides nothing.
trap.counterexample: Z_2 x Z_2 has order 4, is abelian, and has no element of order 4, so it is not cyclic.

check.question: Is Z_2 x Z_3 cyclic, and is Z_2 x Z_4 cyclic?
check.answer: Z_2 x Z_3 is cyclic because gcd(2, 3) = 1 and it is isomorphic to Z_6; Z_2 x Z_4 is not cyclic, since the largest element order is lcm(2, 4) = 4, which is less than 8.
check.explanation: In a direct product the order of an element is the lcm of the component orders. A cyclic group of order n must contain an element of order n, so comparing the largest element order with |G| decides cyclicity in one line.
